svg.title: Figure 2-3: SF-03 at the channel 1 ceiling: a stop from 0.25 m/s against a field sized for 0.20 m/s
svg.desc: Six boxes from the overspeed demand through the monitor window, the logic, the contactors, the coast from 0.25 m/s and the standstill; a time axis to 0.8 s; the field carried as a thin bar over the distance bar the stop from the ceiling needs, with the 0.19 m shortfall hatched red; a floor strip with the robot, the field, the standstill ghost and the person reaching the front.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Figure 2-3 SF-03 at the channel 1 ceiling: a stop from 0.25 m/s against a field sized for 0.20 m/s

svg.text: §2 row SF-03 (window path): 100 + 50 + 20 = 170 ms against the 200 ms target; CFG-001, coast fast planning case a = 0.5 m/s² (unmeasured, WP-V-02); K = 1.6 m/s, Z = 0.1 m, C = 0 (§4.2).

svg.text: At the 0.25 m/s cap (DQ-006 A) the fast coast needs 1.28 m (CK-1b), the slow coast 4.73 m (CK-1a); FS-1b carries 1.09 m: in the planning case the person reaches the robot 0.09 m before it stops.

svg.text: The cap and the trip at limit + 15 % within the 100 ms window bound this case, not the field (§5). Whether FS-1 is sized for the cap is OI-8.

svg.text: Drawn to WP-S-04 v0.2 planning values (t_r 0.17 s, a = 0.5 m/s² unmeasured, C = 0, K = 1.6 m/s). A loop diagram shows the arithmetic of a stop; it does not show that a measure works.
